review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md for the CI-head read, one review per round by SHA, the docs-only Thermo skip; references/review-threads.md for one disposition per thread and naming the sjawhar-agent[bot] thread to the implementer

findings.finding: Acceptance line 1 names only docs/solutions/ as the workflow's own paths, while the live PR file list carries .legion/LEGSMOKE-830/*.json until retro removes them and docs/solutions/ may or may not exist.
findings.answer: Plan §4 A1: a subset predicate (the marker present; every other path .legion/LEGSMOKE-830/ mid-run or docs/solutions/.+-LEGSMOKE-830.md), judged mid-run under the filter with the gap named in Not proven / risk, and for real at C5 and the merge commit; 1 or 1+N files both pass.

findings.finding: Acceptance line 2 states two exclusive end states and the trigger is an out-of-band driver message; every later role must pick the same arm.
findings.answer: Plan §3: the K detector (path, in_reply_to_id==null, review App login, body literal) printed before judging; K≥2 and a post-approval match are reports to the architect; the production check evaluates K at the merged PR.

findings.finding: 'A single line that names this issue' fixes no bytes (apostrophe, suffix, CRLF, BOM, trailing LF) and the spec never names line 2's text.
findings.answer: Plan §1: the 64-byte literal with ASCII apostrophe and dropped run-directory suffix by precedent LEGSMOKE-817; the review line is the plan's literal, quoted verbatim in the reviewer's request; §4 A2 checks wc -c, wc -l, last byte 0a, no 0d, no BOM, whole-file cmp; a request with other wording is a report.

findings.finding: No map from criterion to phase to commit; the head keeps moving after proofs are written, and the head that merges must carry the implementer's own proof.
findings.answer: Plan §2 head table and §4 criterion × phase × head table; the implementer re-proves at C5 (§7.5) and extends its E2E line; every proof headSha names the newest code head of its round.

findings.finding: The proof driver pushes a .fail-me commit onto the issue branch to turn the required gate red; the spec says nothing about who removes it.
findings.answer: Plan §6.4 pre-authorises the implementer's deletion-only cure commit (message, code push, implement App identity, recorded in deviations[]), confined below the approval; a red above C4/C5 is a report, never a push.

findings.finding: Each proof needs a negative control the spec does not name; a control that touches the branch would break A1 or void the approval.
findings.answer: Plan §4: one control per criterion (404 at main before, 404 at BASE after; no-LF/CRLF/wrong-key/wrong-arm/U+2019 cmp variants; #701 and #575 file lists for the allowlist; the measured red commit 57dab69b and the gate logic reproduced locally); no control adds or keeps a path on the branch.

findings.finding: 'Proof is read on GitHub after the merge' never says what production is; merge-gate.md's default would leave Production: pending forever.
findings.answer: Plan §8: main on GitHub is production, the merge is the publish step, no deploy signal or ask is waited on; the exact post-merge reads and the three record places are named.

findings.finding: 'The file at main' is time-indexed on a branch other smoke trees keep moving.
findings.answer: Plan §4 A3 anchors the read to the merge commit M: commits?path=…&sha=main → 1 and M, the file at main and at M, BASE serving 404; unrelated movement of main cannot fail it.

findings.finding: sjawhar-agent[bot] reliably opens an inline thread on the marker file; the spec never mentions it.
findings.answer: Plan §6.2.2: expected; the reviewer answers it as not a defect, names the thread node id to the implementer by envoy_publish, the implementer resolves it with plain gh; an unresolved one is named in the review body, never a stall.

findings.finding: The deployment instruction's waiting rule is not resolved per phase and may split a review round into COMMENT + decision, departing from one review per round.
findings.answer: Plan §5, §6.2, §7, §8 pin which task lines sleep 300 (the implementing task only), which reply WAITING, and that every role acts on the driver's targeted message; §6.2.4 and §9 record the possible two-submission round as a deployment-instruction override, not a spec departure.

findings.finding: The tester's default is to push red tests, but the repository has no harness and any added file breaks acceptance line 1.
findings.answer: Plan §6.1: the tester writes no test file, pushes only test.json, breaks the marker with read-only GitHub probes, and records a defect in failures[]; a compare check proves its push touched only .legion/LEGSMOKE-830/.

findings.finding: The child LEGSMOKE-831 exists in todo with an empty spec and the spec says nothing about it; its handling changes when 830 may be signed off.
findings.answer: Plan §13: 830's branch, PR and proofs assert nothing about 831; A1 and A3 are scoped to this PR, the path and M; release/park/sign-off ordering is the architect's lifecycle decision, which the completion summary names.

findings.finding: Several facts (title bytes, approved version, 831's status, branch head, ruleset, red control, 404 at main) lived only in the context note and were unverified by the analyst.
findings.answer: Plan §11 M1–M10 re-measured each with the planner's own gh/jj/dispatch commands on 2026-10-19 and cites them; none is a product choice.
